**Verdict:** Author's right on depth, reviewer's likely right on bloat. Don't cut to 1,200.

**Why:** Eng-brand authority requires receipts—failure modes, tradeoffs, real metrics, configs. 1,200-word war stories read like marketing fluff, get dismissed by senior devs. High-authority eng blogs (Cloudflare, Discord, Stripe) routinely run 3k–5k words.

**Caveat:** Length ≠ depth. Raw 3,500-word eng drafts usually carry ~30% fat: chronological diary narration, excessive context-setting, dead ends w/o transferable lessons.

**What to do:**
- **Edit for density, not word count.** Cut narrative fluff + filler, keep every hard technical detail (likely lands at 2,200–3,000 words).
- **Front-load value.** Open w/ 150-word TL;DR + architecture diagram + headline numbers (scale, latency, downtime) so skimmers/execs get the win in 60 sec.
- **Make it scannable.** Use specific H2s ("Why dual-writes failed at 40k RPS" vs "The Problem"), diagrams, tables.
- **Split only on natural seams.** 2-part series works if 2 standalone technical problems exist (e.g., data backfill vs zero-downtime cutover); never split on arbitrary word limits.
